title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: Morpholinium can template {W72M12X7} all-inorganic frameworks while buffering pH and filling pores, and Co(II) linkers can be postsynthetically oxidized to unstable Co(III) in a reversible single-crystal transformation.
explanation: One-pot reactions give the Co(II) silicate and germanate frameworks, whereas postsynthetic modification gives the Co(III) analogues. Keggin units adopt 3- and 4-connected modes. Heteroatoms are Si(IV) or Ge(IV) and linking metals include Mn(II/III) or Co(II/III). Redox studies show framework Co(II) oxidized to unstable Co(III) with retention of the single crystal in a reversible transformation.
scope: Heterometal-linked {W72M12X7} polyoxotungstate frameworks with morpholinium countercations.
conditions: One-pot synthesis for Co(II) phases; postsynthetic oxidation for Co(III) phases; morpholinium present as template, buffer, and pore cation.
caveats: The Co(III) state is described as unstable, so the oxidized crystals are not presented as a permanently robust redox form.
